nodes.label: Reconcile running state with server on mount
nodes.rationale: Previously the mount effect set progress but never `running`, so a run already in progress rendered the Start button as available; clicking it reset a live run, producing 'bulk already running' from a button that looked idle. The server is now treated as the authority on whether a run is active.

nodes.label: Poll bulk/status independently of the local batch loop
nodes.rationale: Cron or another browser tab can now advance a run, so this tab must see progress it did not itself cause. Without independent polling, the displayed numbers only moved when this tab's own foreground loop happened to be driving.

nodes.label: Percent read from server rather than computed client-side
nodes.rationale: Two clients each computing their own percentage over different snapshots produced disagreeing figures mid-run, so the server now computes and returns `percent` directly.

nodes.label: bulk-locked response treated as hand-off, not an error
nodes.rationale: A `bulk-locked` error code means cron or another tab already claimed this batch, which is ordinary now that multiple drivers exist. The foreground loop returns silently and lets the independent status poll keep the display current instead of surfacing an error for expected contention.

nodes.label: Start button becomes Resume for a resumable run
nodes.rationale: Resuming continues work the operator already agreed to, so it skips the confirm() warning that a genuinely new run still requires.

nodes.label: Stalled warning explains WP-Cron only fires on site traffic
nodes.rationale: A run can be active with no recent completed batch because background processing relies on WP-Cron, which only runs when someone visits the site; the warning tells the operator to keep the page open or set up a real system cron.

hyperedges.label: BulkPage treats the server as sole source of truth for run state
